newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Wednesday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Wednesday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Wednesday:

Spokesman Joao Vale de Almeida said Commission President Jacques Santer had mentioned in a speech to the European Parliament the risk that the draft Treaty proposed by the Dutch Presidency could be weakened.

Spokesman Patrick Child said the Commission, in cooperation with the European Parliament and the European Monetary Institute, had launched a "euro" barge to explain the practical aspects of the euro. He said it would go from Rotterdam to Strasbourg where it should arrive on July 15, 1997 and be met notably by Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy and EP President Jose Maria Gil Robles.

Vale de Almeida said President Santer would make an official visit to France on Thursday. He said Santer would meet French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin at 0900/0700 GMT and French President Jacques Chirac at 1030/0830 GMT.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/506: Commission decides to pay interest to creditors for overdue payments.
- IP/97/507: Commission issues green paper on supplementary pensions in the Single Market.
- IP/97/508: Commission creates a scientific steering committee (SSC) in the field of consumer health and food safety.
- IP/97/509: Telecom liberalisation in Spain: Commission accepts a short additional period.
- IP/97/511: Commission continues its investigation in to the proposal of P&O and Stena to merge their cross-Channel ferry services.
- Speech/97/136: Speech by Commission President Jacques Santer on "The perspectives of the inter-governmental conference at the Amsterdam European Council".
